articles.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
articles.summary: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.
articles.body:
European airlines have again been hit with a new wave of bomb threats - in the third such incident this week.

On Friday multiple flights to and from Lisbon, Rome, Prague and Sofia were targeted and the threats saw three planes escorted by Hungarian fighter jets, authorities said.

It also saw a number of high-profile media organisations, including Ireland's public broadcaster RTÉ , evacuated after threats were made against them - although there has been no concrete links between the messages against airlines and the broadcasters.

The disruption comes after nearly 30 aircraft and several airports across Europe were impacted by threats earlier this week , in what the UK called a "malicious hoax".

Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats

A Ryanair flight scheduled to leave Lisbon for Rome on Friday was targeted with a threat, the airline said, while at least 11 flights were targeted in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria, according to AFP.

France also reported at least four of its flights were targeted by threats, however they all landed safely.

No explosives have been found on any planes as of Friday.

As airlines were dealing with this latest wave of threats, several media outlets, including RTÉ, were evacuated after similar warnings were made against them.

Staff at the Irish Independent newspaper and the Dublin offices of radio stations NewstalkFM and TodayFM, were also advised to leave their buildings and UK broadcaster Sky said it also received a security threat.

In a statement, gardaí (Irish police) said they were "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe".

While no link has been established between the threats against airlines and media outlets, the Irish government has warned it is a "likely coordinated campaign of disruption".

In a statement, it said: "Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever. It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralised or co-ordinated effort.

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin described situation as "worrying" and added his government's first priority was the safety of the Irish public.

"Yesterday, there appeared to be coordinated efforts to disrupt air travel," he said.

Martin told RTÉ it was not yet known if the threats had come from individuals or if it was a "coordinated attack" but said they were being taken seriously.

Ireland is scheduled to host two high-profile European Union meetings in Dublin next week.

Broadcaster Sky confirmed it had received a security threat, hours after RTÉ had evacuated its building.

The broadcaster, which is owned by Comcast, said in a statement read by a presenter on its news channel that the broadcaster had "carried out a security assessment and reported the matter to the relevant authorities".

"The safety and security of our colleagues is our primary concern, and we are working closely with authorities to ensure our people and operations remain secure."

Friday's disruption comes after the Russian extremist group "Male State", named in this week's hoax bomb threats to Italian airports, denied any link to the false warnings .

Replying to the BBC Russian Service, an account on Telegram - one of several linked to the so-called "Male State" and its founder Vladislav Pozdnyakov - mocked any suggestion the group was involved in emailing the threats.

"What Male State? Where have you seen it? It hasn't existed for many years," the message on the channel reads. "If tomorrow they sign a [threat] letter, say, from Putin, will you then try to reach our president to ask your stupid question?"

articles.title: MP shines in ICAI CA Foundation results, Gwalior’s Vaibhavi, Bhopal’s Harsh secure top ranks
articles.summary: MP leads ICAI CA Foundation Sept 2026: Gwalior’s Vaibhavi Singhal AIR 3 (358/400) and Bhopal’s Harsh Lalwani AIR 11 (349/400).
articles.body: Bhopal: Madhya Pradesh emerged as a major force in the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India’s (ICAI) CA Foundation Examination for September 2026, with Gwalior’s Vaibhavi Singhal securing All India Rank 3 and Bhopal’s Harsh Lalwani secured All India Rank 11.Vaibhavi scored 358 out of 400 marks (89.50 per cent) to claim the third position nationally, her performance placing her just three marks short of the joint first-rank holders, Kansika of Hisar and Mahek Gupta of Hyderabad, who each scored 361 marks (90.25 per cent).Sparsh Khandelwal of Ajmer and J Jayanth of Chennai shared the second rank with 359 marks (89.75 per cent).Vaibhavi’s showing brought pride to Gwalior, placing the city among the country’s leading centres of CA Foundation success.Bhopal’s Harsh secured the first position at the city level with 349 out of 400 marks (87.25 per cent). His score also earned him All India Rank 11, making him one of the stand out performers from the state capital at this year’s examination.The results were declared by the ICAI on Friday. Candidates can access their scorecards through the institute’s official result portal, caresults.icai.org, using their registration and roll numbers.The achievements of both students stood out against an exceptionally competitive national backdrop. Of the 1,04,240 candidates who appeared for the CA Foundation examination, only 19,736 cleared it, yielding an overall pass percentage of 18.93 per cent.The result reflects the demanding nature of the entry-level examination, which tests candidates across accounting, business laws, quantitative aptitude and business economics. In a field where fewer than one in five candidates succeeded, Vaibhavi’s podium finish and Harsh’s city-top rank represent exceptional academic performances.Mentors, coaching institutes and family members congratulated both candidates on their sparkling returns, describing their success as an inspiration for thousands of aspiring chartered accountants across the state. Vaibhavi’s AIR 3 has given new belief to CA aspirants in Gwalior, while Harsh’s top rank at the Bhopal centre has set a new benchmark for those in the state capital.Teachers said their results underline the importance of disciplined preparation, conceptual clarity and consistent practice. With the CA course among the country’s most competitive professional pathways, the performance of Madhya Pradesh students is expected to encourage a larger number of candidates to pursue chartered accountancy.Their remarkable results added to the glitter of Dhanteras celebrations in Gwalior and Bhopal, with the two rank-holders coming out as the latest symbols of Madhya Pradesh’s rising presence in India’s chartered accountancy landscape.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: Amy Acton calls Ramaswamy ad featuring estranged mother ‘terrible and despicable’, has ‘no intention’ of speaking to him
articles.summary: Ohio Governor-elect Amy Acton responds to her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy's controversial campaign ad featuring her estranged mother, calling it 'terrible and despicable.'
articles.body: Ohio Governor-elect Amy Acton has ruled out any conversation with her Republican opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, after his campaign ran an ad featuring her estranged mother, describing the move as “terrible and despicable”In her first television interview since defeating Ramaswamy in Tuesday’s 2026 gubernatorial election, Acton was asked on CBS Mornings whether she had spoken to her former opponent.Ramaswamy had said during his concession speech that he called Acton and left her a message congratulating her on the victory.“I have no intention of speaking to him,” Acton said. “I do believe that leaders' words matter, and we need to hold folks accountable.”The controversy centred on a campaign advertisement featuring Acton's birth mother, Donna Arthur, who called her daughter a “liar”. Acton has been estranged from her mother since she was 12.Acton and her brother were taken out of their mother's care following allegations of sexual abuse by their stepfather, Cledith Arthur, who was arrested and charged with raping Acton when she was between 10 and 12. Her brother later said their mother continued to be married to Arthur until he died in 2004.The advertisement drew criticism from Democrats as well as several prominent Republicans, including Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and Senator Jon Husted. President Donald Trump, however, defended the campaign's decision to run it, calling the advertisement “very powerful” and saying he had urged Ramaswamy not to take it down.Acton said the decision to feature her estranged mother in the campaign was unacceptable. “I would like to say I didn't expect this, but there was no low my opponent wouldn't sink to,” she said, adding that the campaign advertisements had been filled with “lies and hate and vitriol”.She also questioned the motive behind the advertisement, suggesting Ramaswamy had used it because his campaign was struggling. Referring to her birth mother, Acton said it was “clear” that she “was not well”.Calling the advertisement “a terrible and despicable thing to do”, Acton said voters had grown tired of political hostility and wanted elected officials focused on solving problems.“I'm a scrappy kid from Youngstown. I'm not afraid of a fight, but kindness isn't weakness, and that is a big message we saw. People are ready for public service, unity, and decency,” she said.Beyond the campaign controversy, Acton also discussed some of the priorities she intends to pursue as Ohio's next governor.Data centres were among the issues she highlighted during her campaign. She supported a conditional moratorium on new facilities, arguing that their development should not come at the expense of the state's natural resources and communities.Acton said she wanted to protect Ohio's air and water while bringing well-paid union jobs to the state.“We are open for business, but we're not for sale, and we're not to be exploited,” she said.You use AI every day. articles.title: BMC transfers close to 700 engineers in Mumbai through online lottery after cash-for-postings allegations
articles.summary: BMC transfers 695 Mumbai engineers via online lottery system to ensure transparent postings after cash-for-transfer allegations; offline moves only for exceptions.
articles.body: Mumbai: BMC transferred 695 engineers through an online lottery system following allegations of a cash-for-transfer scam last year.Civic officials said the online system, called Employee Transfer System Based on Randomisation, was used for shifting 152 junior engineers, 444 secondary engineers and 99 assistant engineers. “Eligible engineers were allowed to submit between one and five posting preferences and efforts were made to allot preferred postings. Transparency and impartiality were maintained in the transfer and posting process, which has once again shown that there is a positive attitude and satisfaction among the engineering cadre regarding the online process,” an official said.Additional municipal commissioner (eastern suburbs) Avinash Dhakne said most engineers received preferred postings. “This was a fair and transparent process. So now, offline transfers will be exceptions, in cases where there are mid-term transfers. All routine transfers will only take place through the online system. Even with bulk promotions, we will try to do it online only,” he said.The issue resurfaced after BMC ordered the transfer of 165 engineers in 2025. BJP MLA Ameet Satam alleged a cash-for-transfer practice, and the orders were later cancelled on chief minister Devendra Fadnavis’s directions. Later, a committee, headed by the director of engineering services and projects, was set up to carry out periodic transfers in the engineering cadre. The committee subsequently carried out transfers of 169 engineers.Then, two months back, BJP MLA Mihir Kotecha had sought a detailed inquiry by chief secretary Rajesh Agrawal into financial transactions linked to engineers’ transfers.To bring transparency to the process, BMC decided to carry out transfers, promotions and postings in the engineering cadre online. Engineers completing at least three years in one department have to submit their transfer preferences online — minimum one and maximum five preferences. If an employee who has completed three years or more in the same department does not submit their preference online, the system will automatically assign postings according to manpower availability and vacancies. Transfer applications on disability or medical grounds may be submitted offline.RTI activist Anil Galgali, a complainant in the cash-for-transfer controversy, said, “The introduction of the online system marks a significant step towards ensuring transparency, fairness and accountability in BMC’s transfer process. It will also help curb political interference and eliminate undue influence in transfer decisions.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.summary: A 23-year-old Indian woman, identified as Sreeja Koya, has gone missing in Boston, Massachusetts, prompting local police to seek the public's assistance
articles.body: A 23-year-old Indian woman, identified as Sreeja Koya, has gone missing in Boston, Massachusetts, prompting local police to seek the public's assistance in locating her.Koya was reported missing on Tuesday, November 3, after she was last seen leaving her residence in the Edison Green area of Dorchester at around 9:45 pm on Monday, November 2, the Boston Police Department said in a missing-person alert issued on November 4."The Boston Police Department is actively working to locate Sreeja Koya and urges anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to call 911 or contact District C-11 (Dorchester) Detectives at (617) 343-4335," the police statement said.According to the police description, Koya is an Indian woman between 5 feet 3 inches and 5 feet 5 inches tall, with a thin build and black hair. She was last seen wearing a black jacket and blue jeans.Police said she might be in the vicinity of Carson Beach or Harbor Point and urged anyone who may have seen her or has information about her whereabouts to come forward.Koya Sreeja Reddy is a native of Shabdullapuram village in Kanagal mandal of Nalgonda district in Telangana. Sreeja moved to the United States around a year ago to pursue a master's degree. She is studying at the University of Massachusetts Boston and was staying with other Telugu students. Her roommates believed she went for a walk while returning from the birthday celebrations of another friend, but then never returned.Sreeja is the only daughter of Yadagiri Reddy and Roopa, a farmer couple from Shabdullapuram village.
